newsitem.title: JAPAN: WEEK AHEAD - Nikkei vulnerable, may test 19,000.
newsitem.headline: WEEK AHEAD - Nikkei vulnerable, may test 19,000.

text.p: A sharp drop on Wall Street is likely to hurt sentiment in Japan's stock market this week, but the fallout may be limited unless U.S. selling is sustained, analysts said.
Before the 3.1 percent drop in the Dow Jones industrials on Friday, Tokyo traders had expected the benchmark Nikkei index of 225 shares to drift around the 19,000 level.
On Friday, the Nikkei average closed at 19,326.03, down 278.43 points from its close a week earlier, a drop of 1.4 percent.
Analysts said that the Nikkei was now likely to test 19,000. But he said whether it broke through that key barrier next week would depend on how New York fares.

"We'll continue to be cautious over any sharp corrective sales in U.S. stocks, as there are growing concerns about the strong U.S. economy, although it shows few signs of inflation," said Mikio Takada, general manager at Nikko Securities Co Ltd.
But Higashida said there were no clear signs yet that Wall Street's long rally had finally come to an end, and that this latest drop -- like other such falls -- may prove to be a short-term worry.

"The Dow's tumble is likely to hurt sentiment in the market because it will raise concerns that investors with global assets may decrease their holdings in Japanese equities," said Masaaki Higashida, strategist at Nomura Securities.

The Dow tumbled 247.37 points to 7,694.66, marking its second-biggest point drop ever. Friday's slide put the index at its lowest close since June. Tokyo largely recovered from its own sharp fall on Monday when the Nikkei plunged almost four percent.
Domestic issues are also weighing on the Tokyo market, with credit concerns pushing money into a limited number of blue chip shares.
"The recent trend has been that money would flow into a limited number of promising issues, partly due to corporate credit risks," said Shinichi Ichikawa, strategist at Credit Lyonnais Securities.
Worries about corporate credit risks have grown especially in the construction sector since the failure last month of Tokai Kogyo Co Ltd, a major construction group.

Shares of Towa Real Estate Development Co Ltd briefly plunged to a record low of 82 yen on Friday before ending down 41 yen or 31.30 percent at 90 yen, topping the list of percentage losers on the bourse's first section.
Towa's shares were hit by rumours that it is experiencing business difficulties. Officials at the firm were not available to comment on the rumours, due to a company holiday.
The Nikkei has been propped up in part by a rally in high-technology issues. But Ichikawa said there appeared to be little room for a continued rise in the sector.
